blocks.text: How people get access to a Production Hub: Users, named access roles per project, effectivity restrictions, one-off permission overrides, and one accountable Owner with optional Contributors on every work item. Access roles are separate from the authority (approval) roles of the Role register. Clauses quoted from Requirements Prompt v24.6, section 5A and Annex B.6 (confirmed by Daniel, 12 Oct 2026).

Users. Every person who uses a Production Hub shall be a User record with a permanent identifier, name, email, Design Team and Design Sub-team (where applicable), status (Active, Suspended, Left) and a user page. People shall no longer be referenced as free-text names: every owner, contributor, approver, author, attendee and Role register entry shall link to a User. AI agents are not Users and can never hold an access role or an authority.

Access roles. Access is given by named access roles, each bundling a set of permissions. The framework access roles are Admin, Design Lead, Design Authority, Engineer and Viewer (Annex B.6). Access roles are framework-fixed; a project may not add or edit them, but may grant one-off permission overrides (5A.5).

Project assignment. A User shall have access to a project only through a Project Assignment, which records the project, one access role for that project, the validity dates and who assigned it. A User may hold different access roles on different projects. A User with no active assignment to a project shall not see that project's Production Hub data.

Effectivity access. By default a User shall see every effectivity of each project to which they are assigned. An Admin may restrict a Project Assignment to listed effectivities; the user then sees, filters and edits only data whose effectivity overlaps the allowed effectivities, and the effectivity filter (5.25) offers only those; this applies to both viewing and editing (confirmed by Daniel, 12 Oct 2026). Data with no effectivity (for example EDRs, TSMs and framework pages) is not restricted.

Permission overrides. An Admin may grant or deny a single permission to a User on a project, in addition to the permissions of the access role, with a reason, an expiry date (optional) and the approving Admin recorded. A deny override prevails over the role. Overrides shall be listed on the admin page and on the user page.

Access roles and authority roles. Access roles control what a User may see and edit in the Hub. The authority roles of the Role register (6C.14, Annex B.4) control who may approve, agree, break and release, over a stated area. The two are separate: an authority role assignment shall require an active Project Assignment on that project whose access role includes the matching approval permission (Design Lead access role for a Design Lead authority, Design Authority access role for a Design Authority authority; Admin may hold either). The approval roles Technical Authority for Design, Design Approver and Discipline Lead have no access role of their own and are held on top of the Engineer access role (or Admin). The software shall check both at the date of each decision. Confirmed by Daniel, 12 Oct 2026.

Owner and contributors. Every work item (FDPS, Issue, Action, Lesson Learned, Design Review, Hub Page, Requirement Document, TSM, Verification, Risk and any task record) shall have exactly one accountable Owner, a User, and may have any number of Contributors, also Users. The Owner shall hold an active Project Assignment with edit permission for the item's data type. Ownership changes shall be recorded with who changed it and when. Sub-system and Sub-structure pages keep the derived owner of 5.30 (the Design Lead from the Role register, itself a User).

Admin page. Each Production Hub shall have an admin page, visible only to Users holding the Admin access role on that project, or to a framework administrator, who administers users across all projects (both kept, confirmed by Daniel, 12 Oct 2026), with: a searchable, filterable list of Users (name, Design Team, project, access role, effectivity access, overrides, status, last active); an edit panel per User to add or end Project Assignments, set the access role per project, restrict effectivities, add or remove permission overrides and suspend the User; and an audit trail of every access change. Access changes take effect immediately and are logged as Change Records of type Access change.

User pages. Each User shall have a user page. In this version it shows only the name, Design Team and Sub-team, status, access role per project with effectivity access, authority roles from the Role register, and the items for which the User is Owner or Contributor, grouped by data type. Further content is to be defined.

Permissions. Permissions are per data type and action: View, Create, Edit, Approve (per the authority checks of 6C.14), Release, Administer users. The permission bundle of each access role is set out in Annex B.6.
Annex B.6 access role Admin: Everything an Engineer can do; administer users, Project Assignments, effectivity restrictions and permission overrides on the project (5A.8); view the audit trail.
Annex B.6 access role Design Lead: Engineer permissions; may hold Design Lead authority roles (5A.6); approve EDR line-item breaks and interface breaks within the Role register area.

Annex B.6 access role Design Authority: Engineer permissions; may hold Design Authority authority roles (5A.6); approve TSM statement breaks and bulk-confirm TSM supersessions within the area; approve for release where delegated.

Annex B.6 access role Engineer: View all project data within the allowed effectivities; create and edit FDPSs, line-item reviews, compliance, verifications, issues, actions, lessons and pages they own or contribute to; raise review flags.
Annex B.6 access role Viewer: View only, within the allowed effectivities; may comment and use the AI bar.
